Apple today updated its "obsolete" and "vintage" product lists, with the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X now classified as vintage products. Details below.

The 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X are now classified as vintage products

Apple today updated a support article titled "Obtaining service for your Apple product after the warranty expires," moving the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X from the "obsolete products" list to the "vintage products" list.

Apple notes that once a product is placed on the vintage list, the company will cease providing all hardware repair services, and authorised repair centres will no longer be able to order parts for it.

Products are generally classified as vintage more than seven years after Apple discontinues their sale, though the actual timing of the classification remains at Apple's discretion.

Meanwhile, products on Apple's "obsolete products" list will only receive repairs while parts remain available. So-called "obsolete products" are those that Apple has stopped selling for more than five but less than seven years.

Apple dropped major operating system support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with iOS 16 being its last major release. The device currently supports up to iOS 16.7.16. As for the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro, it only supports up to macOS Sequoia, and can currently be upgraded to macOS 15.7.7.

For the full list of Apple's "obsolete" and "vintage" products, as well as special circumstances where certain products may receive repair services for up to 10 years, click here to view.
